title: NCP: Verifier-Guided Optimization of Weight-Space Control Policies. Toward Recursive Self-Improvement through Neural Flow Rules
domain: inference-time weight interventions; recursive self-improvement framework; arithmetic reasoning microbenchmark

headline_result.text: The best of three deterministically synthesized weight interventions cut validation token repetition from 0.4133 to 0.2191 with a -0.0574% perplexity change, but none produced a newly correct answer, so all three were archived and the active policy stayed empty.
headline_result.quote: One projection reduced validation token repetition from 0.4133 to 0.2191, with a perplexity change of -0.0574%. All candidates produced zero newly correct exact answers

key_claims.claim: NCP is a closed-loop controller that synthesizes, verifies and admits temporary weight-space intervention rules while restoring base parameters after each request.
key_claims.quote: synthesizes candidate weight-space intervention rules, evaluates them, and maintains a versioned table of admitted policies.

key_claims.claim: Candidate synthesis in the recorded experiment is a deterministic Python procedure, not an LLM editor.
key_claims.quote: Its current synthesis step is a deterministic Python procedure driven by observed task labels and captured activations.

key_claims.claim: All three candidates passed the perplexity budget but none corrected an answer, so the active table stayed at zero rules.
key_claims.quote: All three candidates met the configured perplexity budget. The corrected-answer threshold was one; the active table consequently remained at zero rules.

key_claims.claim: Final held-out test accuracy was 0/3 for both original and routed execution.
key_claims.quote: Final exact-answer scoring was 0/3 for both original and routed execution.

key_claims.claim: Fresh-process repetition and saved-table resumption reproduced the recorded outcomes.
key_claims.quote: Fresh-process repetition and saved-table resumption reproduced the measured outcomes.

limitations_stated.text: The evaluation is a nine-question handwritten architectural microbenchmark with bounded corpus slices.
limitations_stated.quote: The nine-question handwritten fixture is an architectural microbenchmark of telemetry, candidate generation, admission and persistence.

notes_for_review: An engineering framework (flow table, verifier, admission gate) that credits Takehi et al. as its conceptual basis, but no LLM proposes or writes weights: candidates come from a deterministic diff-of-means/ablation template. The only experiment is a 9-question fixture on SmolLM-135M with 3 test questions, and no candidate was admitted, so it shows the plumbing works rather than any improvement. Code is said to be MIT-licensed but no repository link is given.
